subject: VPC licensing: floating credits vs fixed commit — concession options
messages:
From: Cara Nguyen <cara.nguyen@solacehealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@solacehealth.com
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VPC pricing — ask: flexible credits vs fixed commit (budget constraints)

Hi Mateo / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed by the latency numbers and the rollout path. We’re kicking off procurement and need two clear commercial options to present to our CFO tomorrow: one that minimizes upfront spend (we have a tight Q2 cash plan) and one that minimizes unit cost for steady-state usage. Key questions:

- Can you give a clear comparison between a fixed node-commit (3yr / 24mo amortized) vs a floating-credit model (elastic tranches)?
- Is the platform fee mandatory for private deploys, or can it be amortized/waived for a pilot?
- What are the support tiers and SLA differences (response vs on-call cadence + incident credits)?
- Any room for credits for the pilot period (we expect 2 months of POC traffic)?

Attached is our procurement template and usage forecast (pilot + scale assumptions). We’d prefer a short bulleted matrix so the CFO can see the tradeoffs quickly.

Also note payment terms: Solace typically asks for 45–60 day net terms for new vendors. Is that possible?

Appreciate a concise reply — can you send options by EOD?

Best,
Cara Nguyen
Head of Platform Procurement
Solace Health
procurement@solacehealth.com
Attachments: solace-procurement-template.xlsx (referenced)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Cara Nguyen <cara.nguyen@solacehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VPC pricing — ask: flexible credits vs fixed commit (budget constraints)

Cara — thanks, and great to hear the demo landed well. Quick summary below (high level numbers are illustrative; detailed workbook attached):

Option 1 — Fixed commit (predictable, lowest unit cost)
- Structure: 24-month commit for N dedicated nodes (prepaid).
- Platform fee: one-time platform entitlement; we can amortize across 18 months on the quote.
- Support: Gold (24/7 on-call, 1hr P1 initial response, monthly SRE cadence).
- Commercial impact: ~18–22% discount vs list on per-token/unit basis.
- Best for: predictable steady-state or customers that want predictable OPEX.

Option 2 — Floating credits (elastic, less upfront)
- Structure: elastic tranche model — prebuy a credit bucket (6–12 month tranches) and draw down; unused credits roll forward for 90 days.
- Platform fee: refundable credit up to 50% against first-year draw if you convert to committed term within 12 months.
- Support: Silver (business-hours on-call, 4hr P1) with option to add SRE retainer.
- Commercial impact: unit pricing ~10–14% off list; more flexible but higher steady-state cost.
- Best for: customers with variable bursty workloads or limited upfront budget.

Pilot concessions we can offer (conditional):
- Two pilot months waived up to $40k (applies to platform fee or usage units, whichever is used first).
- Amortize platform fee over 18 months on the invoice for accounting friendliness.
- Reduce SRE retainer by 25% for first 12 months if you commit to a 24-month minimum term.

Open items for us to confirm for the formal quote:
- Exact node counts / usage bands from your forecast (we looked at the sheet but need confirmation).
- Desired payment terms (45 vs 60 days).
- Any legal must-haves for the SOW (export controls / data residency addenda).

I’ve attached a concise term-sheet and a draft SOW for your review: redwood-privdeploy-term-sheet-v1.pdf, SOW-draft.docx, pricing-comparison.xlsx. If these options look good I’ll work with Marissa (commercial ops) to produce a DocuSign-ready quote.

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Sales Director, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Attach: redwood-privdeploy-term-sheet-v1.pdf; SOW-draft.docx; pricing-comparison.xlsx

From: Tom Ellison <tom.ellison@solacehealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Cara Nguyen <cara.nguyen@solacehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VPC pricing — ask: flexible credits vs fixed commit (budget constraints)

Mateo / Marissa — thanks for the clear options. A couple of clarifying items before we present to finance: 

1) SRE retainer: can you confirm what activities are covered (on-call, runbook updates, incident postmortem)? If we take the 25% reduction for year one, do you allow banked hours to be consumed in month 13–18?

2) Pilot credits: are the two pilot months a true credit (no invoicing) or a deferral? Our auditors want a clean credit applied to the invoice rather than a delayed charge.

3) Payment terms: Solace will push for net-60 for the initial year. Any flexibility for milestone invoicing (40% up front, remainder upon pilot acceptance) to bridge cashflow?

4) Legal: our counsel will push a 30-day SLA cure window on service credits — is that acceptable?

On quoting — we should see the amortized schedule in the quote line items so finance can model the P&L. If you can incorporate the amortization and the pilot credit as explicit line items in the pricing workbook that will help.

Onward,
Tom Ellison
VP Engineering
Solace Health
Tom.Ellison@solacehealth.com

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellison <tom.ellison@solacehealth.com>, Cara Nguyen <cara.nguyen@solacehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VPC pricing — ask: flexible credits vs fixed commit (budget constraints)

Tom / Cara — appreciate the fast feedback. Short answers and commitments below — we’ll turn this into a revised term sheet and DocuSign quote by EOD tomorrow.

1) SRE retainer: covers 8 hours/month of proactive work (runbook updates, configuration tuning, monthly health check) and on-call rotation for P1/P2 escalation. Incident postmortems included for P1 events. Banked hours: yes, up to 3 months of unused retainer hours can be banked and are usable through month 18.

2) Pilot credits: we will apply a true credit against invoices (not a deferral). Pilot credit: two months or up to $40k, whichever is lower — shown as a credit line on the invoice.

3) Payment terms / milestone invoicing: we can support milestone invoices (40% upon signature, 50% on pilot acceptance, 10% on GA) and will accept net-60 on the remaining 60% tranche for the initial year.

4) SLA cure window: 30-day cure window for credit remediation is acceptable. Service credits will be capped as per the Gold/Silver table in the term sheet.

Commercial concessions (confirmed):
- Platform fee amortized over 18 months on the invoice (explicit line items).
- 25% first-year SRE retainer discount if you sign a 24-month commit within 30 days of this email.
- Two pilot months credited up to $40k as an invoice credit.

Next steps: Marissa will push a revised pricing workbook and DocuSign quote (includes amortization schedule and pilot credit line) — can you confirm final node counts and preferred milestone schedule by close of day tomorrow so we can lock the quote?

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Sales Director, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
